items.title: 63477_Joe Darensbourg oral history interview
items.q: The band that I left Opelousas with, Dr. Moon Medicine Company it was called, was owned by a millionaire -- and his name was Doctor Moon.

ctx.x: Not always. The band that I left Opelousas with, Dr. Moon Medicine Company it was called, was owned by a millionaire -- and his name was Doctor Moon. I don't know I think they called him Frank or whatever. But I never called him anything...nobody called him anything but Dr. Moon.
What was the purpose of you going with them?

items.title: Joe Darensbourg and Minor "Ram" Hall Interview, 1957-04-18
items.q: Dr. Moon offered me a job. He wanted me to play a saxophone and clarinet. So, Dr. Moon bought me a saxophone.

ctx.x: At this time, you were playing only clarinet, huh? That's right.

And finally, uh, a medicine show came through Opelousa's, Dr. Moon. That's what you hear me talking about all the time. So, Dr. Moon offered me a job. He wanted me to play a saxophone and clarinet. So, Dr. Moon bought me a saxophone. Cause I didn't have no room.

items.title: Joe Darensbourg and Minor "Ram" Hall Interview, 1957-04-18

ctx.x: He says, we do not serve colored people. He says, oh, no. No. No. No. No. So, Joe, uh, what, what do you do after you, after O.C., uh, what's his name? What's his name? What's that, O.T.O.S.?

The Toothjohnker? Toothjohnker. Well, I left, uh, Baton Rouge and went to work, uh, my brother and I got a little job playing a, uh, kind of a Catholic convention in a little town named Opelousa, Louisiana, and we took a band over there, and I went to work with a, a family band. I stayed, uh, a fellow named, uh, Martell's Officer, called Louisiana Ramblers.
They offered me this job, and, uh, I stayed and worked with them.
